name: Sukhbaatar and Chinggis Square
tagline: Government Palace, museums and every cafe in walking range
description: The political and cultural core sits around Chinggis Square, ringed by the Government Palace, national museums, the opera house and the city's densest run of cafes and restaurants. Embassies and business hotels fill the surrounding blocks, and almost everything a visitor needs is inside a 15-minute walk.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads who want to work from cafes and walk to everything.
pros: Most walkable part of the city
Embassies, banks and museums all close
cons: Severe winter air pollution from coal smoke
Traffic gridlock on the ring roads

name: Zaisan, Khan-Uul
tagline: Riverside towers under the memorial hill
description: Tucked against the Bogd Khan mountain south of the Tuul river, Zaisan is the expat and affluent-local enclave: newer apartment complexes, international schools, western supermarkets and cocktail bars. Elevation and distance from the ger districts mean noticeably cleaner winter air than the city core.
bestFor: Nomads staying a winter who prioritise air quality and modern apartments.
pros: Best winter air quality in the city
Hiking trails start at the edge of the district
cons: Feels like an expat bubble, little local life
Long, jammed commute into the centre

name: Bayangol
tagline: Malls, mid-rise flats and a sensible middle price
description: West of the centre along Peace Avenue, Bayangol mixes Soviet-era housing with newer mid-rise blocks, plus shopping centres, the Ramada and a good supply of local restaurants. It is the usual compromise district: cheaper than Sukhbaatar, still a short ride or a long walk from the square.
bestFor: Nomads wanting central-ish access without paying Sukhbaatar or Zaisan rents.
pros: Good value compared with the centre
Buses along Peace Avenue run frequently
cons: Winter smog is as bad as the centre
Older blocks vary a lot in heating quality

name: Sansar, Bayanzurkh
tagline: Quiet eastern blocks with parks and cheap rent
description: Sansar sits east of the centre in Bayanzurkh, a settled residential pocket of apartment blocks around the 13th khoroolol with schools, small parks and neighbourhood shops. Rents fall clearly below the centre, and the National Amusement Park and Ulaanbaatar's larger green spaces are within reach.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a normal local neighbourhood at a lower rent.
pros: Calm residential streets and local shops
Reasonable bus links along the main road
cons: Nothing much to do without heading into town

name: Chingeltei
tagline: The cheapest option, right where the ger districts start
description: Directly north of the centre, Chingeltei runs from apartment blocks near Peace Avenue up into the hillside ger districts. The lower blocks are the cheapest walkable-to-centre housing in the city, with the Narantuul-style street markets and everyday local life that comes with it.
bestFor: Bare-budget nomads who want walking distance to the centre for the lowest rent.
pros: Lowest rents near the city centre
cons: Worst winter air pollution, coal smoke drifts down from the ger districts
